title: Jailer 2 Becomes Kollywood's First 2026 Film With Rs 100 Crore ROI
excerpt: Koimoi reports the Rajinikanth-led Tamil film has returned Rs 109.35 crore over its estimated Rs 350 crore budget in 19 days, on tracker estimates.
body:
• Koimoi reports Jailer 2 has recorded a return on investment of Rs 109.35 crore in 19 days, becoming Kollywood's first film of 2026 to cross Rs 100 crore in ROI, on the tracker's reported estimates.
  • The Tamil-language, Rajinikanth-led film has earned Rs 459.35 crore net in India against an estimated budget of Rs 350 crore, according to Koimoi; Sacnilk puts India net slightly higher at Rs 459.70 crore.
  • On Day 19 the film added Rs 3.4 crore net in India, and its worldwide gross stands at Rs 812 crore on Sacnilk's estimates.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has passed a profitability milestone that matters more to its makers than a gross total. According to Koimoi's Day 19 report, the film has recorded a return on investment of Rs 109.35 crore, making it Kollywood's first film of 2026 to enjoy an ROI of Rs 100 crore. The figures are the tracker's reported estimates, not studio-confirmed accounts.

Jailer 2 is a Tamil-language action-comedy thriller directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Kalanithi Maran's Sun Pictures, Koimoi reports. Rajinikanth leads a cast that also includes SJ Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu, Ramya Krishnan and Vidya Balan in key roles. It was released on October 15, 2026, and is the sequel in the Jailer franchise.

How the ROI figure is built

Koimoi presents the calculation plainly. The film was made at an estimated budget of Rs 350 crore and has earned Rs 459.35 crore net at the Indian box office in 19 days, which the tracker equates to Rs 542.05 crore gross. Subtract the budget from the India net and the result is the Rs 109.35 crore ROI. Calculated further, Koimoi says the film is enjoying 31.24% returns and, on its parameters, has secured a plus verdict.

"According to Koimoi's Day 19 report , the film has recorded a return on investment of Rs 109.35 crore, making it Kollywood's first film of 2026 to enjoy an ROI of Rs 100 crore."

A second tracker lands in the same place on the running total, with a small difference in the final decimal. Sacnilk's Day 19 report puts India net at Rs 459.70 crore and India gross at Rs 537.75 crore, with overseas gross at Rs 274.25 crore and worldwide gross at Rs 812 crore. Readers should treat both sets as reported trade estimates; small differences between trackers are normal during a run.

Day 19 and the week behind it

On its third Monday, Day 19, the film scored Rs 3.4 crore net in India, Koimoi reports, a drop of 38.18% compared with Day 16's Rs 5.5 crore, which the tracker describes as a good hold. Sacnilk reports the same Day 19 total of Rs 3.40 crore across 7,995 shows, led by the Tamil version at Rs 2.20 crore, followed by Hindi at Rs 60 lakh, Telugu at Rs 43 lakh and Kannada at Rs 17 lakh.

https://x.com/NewsWireLK/status/2117187461013238212

Koimoi's week-wise India net breakdown shows where the total was built: Week 1 brought Rs 334.35 crore over eight days, Week 2 added Rs 95.55 crore, and Days 16 to 19 added Rs 5.5 crore, Rs 9.35 crore, Rs 11.2 crore and Rs 3.4 crore respectively. The bulk of the recovery, in other words, came in the opening week, and the film crossed its estimated budget in India net terms well before the third weekend.

What this milestone does and does not say

This is a new development, separate from the worldwide gross story. The Videshi reported on November 1 that the film had crossed Rs 800 crore worldwide, a first for Tamil cinema. The ROI milestone answers a different question: not how much money passed through ticket windows worldwide, but whether the India net collection alone has moved clearly past the production budget the tracker assigns to the film. On Koimoi's numbers, it has, by more than Rs 100 crore.

Koimoi notes that from here it will be a wait-and-watch situation regarding the film's entry into the Rs 500 crore net club in India. That would require roughly another Rs 40 crore net from a run whose weekday pace is now in low single digits, even after a stronger third Sunday. The tracker also says the film is expected to churn out more numbers with some fuel left in the tank. For diaspora viewers, the film remains in theatres in its Tamil version and in Hindi, Telugu and Kannada versions, as Sacnilk's language-wise Day 19 figures show.
